title: Unit – 1 : Session – 12 : SLO – 1 | Dynamic Dispatch & Overhead
sections: 1) class Base { void show(){ System.out.println("Base"); } }  class Derived extends Base { @Override void show(){ System.out.println("Derived"); } }  Base b = new Derived(); b.show(); → prints Derived (dynamic dispatch via base reference).

2) Virtual method table (vtable): each class with overridable methods has a table mapping method slots to implementations; an object stores a pointer to its class's vtable. For Base b = new Derived(); b.show(); the JVM reads Derived's vtable entry for show() and jumps to Derived.show — this is how overriding is resolved at run time.

3) Direct vs virtual call: a direct (static/private/final) call binds at compile time — the address is fixed, so it is faster and inlinable. A virtual call must load the vtable pointer and index the table at run time — a small overhead (extra indirection, harder to inline), in exchange for polymorphic flexibility.
